clue.text: Harry can prepare a king's shed — look!

indicators.note: to harry is to harass and disturb, so these letters are thrown out of their order
shed means cast off, so the king's letter is dropped from the jumbled pool

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for king (Latin rex)

explanation.surface: An order to watch as someone harasses a king's outbuilding.
explanation.walkthrough: CAN PREPARE A has eleven letters; 'shed' throws out one R (king), and 'Harry' rearranges the remaining ten into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's look is their outward appearance, a straightforward noun synonym.

clue.text: Pull everyone on river

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sitting on another is placed above it

parts.note: everyone means all
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, England

explanation.surface: An instruction to get everybody hauling on a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Allure is attraction, the pull something exerts on people, used as a noun.

clue.text: Some forgot a topper, upsetting King Edward

indicators.note: in a down clue, upsetting tips the letters over so they read from the bottom up
some of the following words supplies the letters, a run tucked inside them

explanation.surface: Someone forgot a hat, embarrassing a King Edward.
explanation.walkthrough: King Edward looks like a monarch who mislaid his crown; it is a well-known British variety of potato. The letters OTATOP sit inside 'forgot a topper' and read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: King Edward is a popular floury British variety of the vegetable, so this is a definition by example.

clue.text: Mean strangers spoiled deals

indicators.note: spoiled means ruined, so these letters are wrecked and reassembled

parts.note: the setter's fodder; read as MEAN STRANGER, one S fewer, it rearranges exactly

explanation.surface: Unkind strangers wrecked some agreements.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder has one S too many: MEAN STRANGER rearranges exactly into the answer, so the printed plural is a slip.
explanation.definitionFit: Deals are agreements struck between parties, which are also called arrangements.

clue.text: Turn over after the Parisian raised voice

indicators.note: after says the turnover piece follows the French article
in a down clue, raised lifts the letters so they read from the bottom up

parts.note: la is French for the, as a Parisian would say it
T/O is the standard abbreviation for turnover

explanation.surface: Someone turns over after a Parisian lifts their voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised voice' looks like a phrase, but 'raised' works on LA, giving AL, followed by TO, the abbreviation for turnover.
explanation.definitionFit: The alto is a singing voice, the part lying just below the soprano in a choir.

clue.text: Yells and races off without thinking

indicators.note: off means gone bad or out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wild person shouts and dashes away heedlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something carelessly means doing it heedlessly, with no thought given to it.

clue.text: Head of university wearing the chap's shades

indicators.note: the chap's letters wear the first letter, i.e. go around it like clothing

parts.note: the chap's is he's, written as HES

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A university head puts on the man's sunglasses.
explanation.walkthrough: Shades looks like sunglasses that are worn; here it means colours.
explanation.definitionFit: Shades are tints or colours, the same thing as hues.

clue.text: Dirty punch as teenager boxes?

indicators.note: boxes means contains, so the words punch as teenager hold the answer inside them

explanation.surface: Asks whether a dirty punch is what a fighting teenager throws.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxes' suggests a teenage boxer; it actually means the clue words contain the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Unchaste means sexually impure, and dirty is used in that lewd sense.

clue.text: Barrier to cakes getting prepared without tip from Delia

indicators.note: without means outside, so the jumbled letters go around the other piece
prepared means made ready, as in cooking, so the letters are rearranged
the tip of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A cook's obstacle: cakes being made without a hint from Delia.
explanation.walkthrough: Delia Smith is a famous British TV cook, which makes 'prepared' read as baking; 'without' here means outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: A stockade is a defensive enclosure of upright posts, a kind of protective fence.

clue.text: Retail true rubbish? That's what you get from bookshops

definitions.text: That's what you get from bookshops

indicators.note: rubbish means worthless or poorly made, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Questions whether shop rubbish is the product of booksellers.
explanation.definitionFit: Bookshops sell written works, which are collectively called literature.

clue.text: Italian author capturing husband's parrot

indicators.note: capturing means holding, so the author's name goes around the other letter

parts.note: Umberto Eco was an Italian novelist

explanation.surface: An Italian writer catches a married man's pet bird.
explanation.walkthrough: Parrot looks like a noun, the bird; it is the verb meaning to repeat.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot words is to repeat them mindlessly, which is what an echo does.

clue.text: Gain respect

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a rise in value, as of shares or property
second meaning: admiration and esteem for someone

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like an instruction to earn respect; the two words are separate meanings of one noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers both an increase in an asset's worth and the regard or recognition given to someone.

clue.text: Set of drinks including Tango makes you plump

indicators.note: including means containing, so the drinks hold the other letter

parts.note: a round is one set of drinks bought for a group
T is Tango in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Drinking rounds of Tango, a fizzy British soft drink, will fatten you up.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotund describes a rounded, plump figure, a synonym for chubby.

clue.text: Stir sailor's food

parts.note: a stir or flap is a state of excited agitation
jack, as in jack tar, is a sailor

explanation.surface: Mix up a seaman's dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: Stir looks like a verb for mixing food; it is a noun meaning a fuss. A flapjack is a British oat-and-syrup bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A flapjack is a baked oat bar (or in the US a pancake), an example of something to eat.

clue.text: Even short relative enters happy

indicators.note: enters means goes into, so the relative goes inside the other word

parts.note: happy means content
sis is short for sister

explanation.surface: A shortish relative comes in, perfectly cheerful.
explanation.definitionFit: Even means steady and uniform, as does consistent.

clue.text: Protested as Republican showed Democrat out

indicators.note: out means gone away, so the Democrat letter is removed

parts.note: showed means demonstrated

explanation.surface: A Republican complained about showing a Democrat the door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' removes the first D from DEMONSTRATED, leaving EMONSTRATED.
explanation.definitionFit: To remonstrate is to argue in protest, so protested is its synonym in the past tense.

clue.text: Second wife permits drinks

parts.note: permits means allows

explanation.surface: A second wife lets someone have drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Drinks, as a verb, means swallows: takes liquid down the throat.

clue.text: Old princess's style creating scandal

parts.note: Di was the late Princess Diana; her possessive gives DIS
grace is elegance or style

explanation.surface: A former princess's elegance causes a public outcry.
explanation.definitionFit: A disgrace is a shameful affair, the same as a scandal.

clue.text: I could be clueless with this problem

definitions.text: I could be clueless with this problem

parts.words: I could be clueless with this problem
parts.note: the speaker is a setter or author who cannot produce clues or words at all

explanation.walkthrough: Clueless sounds like stupid; for a crossword setter it means unable to write any clues.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer's inability to produce work is a well-known creative blockage.

clue.text: Nick turned up in low country

indicators.note: in places the reversed word inside the other

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up makes the letters read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: nick and can are both slang for prison

explanation.surface: A prison rises up in a low-lying country.
explanation.walkthrough: Low looks like an adjective (the Low Countries are the Netherlands and Belgium); it is the verb for a cow's call. Nick and can are both slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Monaco is a tiny independent principality on the Riviera, a European state.

clue.text: Barrister put on small underwear

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece put on another sits above it

parts.note: a brief is slang for a barrister or lawyer

explanation.surface: A lawyer dresses in skimpy underpants.
explanation.definitionFit: Briefs are short close-fitting underpants.

clue.text: Betrayed sea captain leaving British trial most pale

indicators.note: leaving means departing, so the British letter is removed

parts.note: Captain William Bligh of HMS Bounty was betrayed by his mutinous crew
a test is a trial

explanation.surface: A betrayed captain drops a British case, looking very wan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes the B out of BLIGH, leaving LIGH.
explanation.definitionFit: Light colours are pale ones, so the superlative means palest.

clue.text: Left work

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the ... Party, Britain's main left-wing party

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as having quit a job; the two words are separate meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names Britain's left-of-centre political party and also means toil or effort.

clue.text: Liberal — one politician lacking firmness

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A single Liberal MP shows no backbone.
explanation.definitionFit: Limp means floppy, without stiffness or rigidity.

clue.text: Something you might fail? Not oddly your fault

indicators.note: not taking the odd letters means taking the even ones, the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: Failing something is not, strangely, the fault of the person addressed.
explanation.definitionFit: An oral is a spoken examination, a test a student could fail.

clue.text: Large emperor geese primarily imitate cuckoo sound

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so each word gives its opening letter
cuckoo means crazy, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Big emperor geese try to copy the call of a cuckoo.
explanation.walkthrough: Sound looks like a noise; it is the adjective meaning valid. Cuckoo looks like the bird, but here it scrambles IMITATE into ITIMATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound argument is valid and well founded, which is what legitimate means.

clue.text: Look for well-groomed missing student

indicators.note: missing means lacking, so the student letter is removed

parts.note: sleek means smooth and well-groomed
L is a learner, i.e. a student

explanation.surface: Searching for a tidy student who has disappeared.
explanation.definitionFit: To seek is to search, the same as to look for.

clue.text: Brilliant writer hugged by boss old American

indicators.note: hugged by means held inside, so the writer goes into the boss

parts.note: a boss or stud is a raised knob or ornament
a pen is a writing instrument
US means American

explanation.surface: A writer embraced by an elderly American employer.
explanation.walkthrough: Boss looks like an employer; it is a stud, a raised ornamental knob.
explanation.definitionFit: Stupendous means astonishingly good or impressive, a synonym for marvellous.
